specifications.name: Published specification
specifications.scale_label: difference in injuries per intersection per year
components: corridor locations on the treated corner's own streets
unweighted mean of per unit changes in an annual injury count, one sample t test
30.0 m in the reproduction, because the published specification does not state one
specifications.estimator_detail: For each treated unit i, take the count inside the after window and the count inside the before window, put each on an annual footing by multiplying by 12 and dividing by the number of months in the window, and take the difference. Do the same at each of that unit's own comparison locations and average over them. The unit's value is the first minus the second. The estimate is the unweighted mean over units, the standard error is the sample standard deviation divided by the square root of the unit count, and the test is a one sample t test against zero on n minus 1 degrees of freedom.
specifications.placebo_detail: The published specification publishes no placebo. The reproduction runs one on the same cells, which is how the two failing cells in the first column group were found.
specifications.coverage: six published cells over two outcomes, both of which are injuries to people

ambiguities.ambiguity: DOT does not say which three intersections along a street are kept when more than three qualify.
ambiguities.choice: The three nearest to the study corner by straight line distance, with a stable sort so ties keep gazetteer order. Keeping the nearest three makes the comparison as local as DOT's own words about localized injury trends imply.

ambiguities.ambiguity: DOT does not say whether the three are counted per street or per direction along a street.
ambiguities.choice: Per street, so all three can fall on the same side of the study corner. The alternative, three in each direction, would double the group on a two way corridor and is not what the sentence says.

ambiguities.ambiguity: DOT does not define distance, which could be measured along the street network or straight.
ambiguities.choice: Straight line distance in the project's local metric projection. Because a candidate is on the study corner's own street, the two agree closely except where that street curves.

ambiguities.ambiguity: DOT does not say what identifies a street of the daylit intersection.
ambiguities.choice: The gazetteer names of pairs standing within 25 m of the treated position, together with the pairs snapped to that corner's own node. Two readings are unioned because a treatment point and the node the gazetteer chose are not always the same node where a junction carries several.

ambiguities.ambiguity: Street names repeat across the city, so BROADWAY or 3 AVE names several corridors.
ambiguities.choice: A candidate must lie in the same borough as the study corner, taken from the universe intersection rather than from the gazetteer borough column, which is empty on 4,143 pairs. Set same_borough to False to drop the restriction.

ambiguities.ambiguity: DOT does not say whether a corner reachable along two of the study corner's streets counts twice.
ambiguities.choice: Once, at its shortest distance, because DOT averages outcomes across comparison locations rather than across street slots.

ambiguities.ambiguity: DOT excludes locations with other interventions from the daylit side as well as the comparison side, and dates that exclusion to its analysis period.
ambiguities.choice: Only the comparison side is screened here, and without a date, because build_controls() is handed a treated frame that the caller has already chosen and because most treatment families in this repository carry a date precision coarser than the month. Screening the treated side belongs to whoever builds the subset, and the count of units left with no controls is reported so the loss is visible.

ambiguities.ambiguity: DOT's phrase non-daylit is narrower than the phrase any other roadway interventions in the next sentence.
ambiguities.choice: The broader reading, any treatment of any family at any date within 30 m, which is the project's own convention for a clean comparison. It costs candidates: 26,200 of 48,266 universe intersections carry something within 30 m, against 7,432 under a daylighting only reading.

specifications.comparison_rule: NYC DOT's published comparison rule, reproduced so that our estimates are comparable to theirs. For each treated corner, the streets meeting at it are read from the gazetteer, each street is walked outward, and up to three untreated intersections along that street within 1 mile are taken as controls, ordered by distance from the study corner.
specifications.comparison_exclusion: A candidate must have no treatment of any family from data/treatments.csv within 30 m, at any date. This is broader than DOT's screen, which named five features, either an Open Street, a hardened daylighting treatment, a No Standing Anytime sign, a protected bike lane or a completed Street Improvement Project, and applied only to installations inside the analysis period. Pass clean_families to narrow it.

The specification path panel shows how much each of those changes moves the estimate.

specifications.name: Falsification tested specification
components: the same admissible span as the extended record, per subset
36 months before and up to 24 after, with the after period chosen per subset by right censoring
three matched comparison intersections per treated unit
fixed effects Poisson with unit and calendar month effects, cluster robust variance of type CRV1 on the match group
whichever of the five outcomes is selected
30.0 m, with a 300.0 m spillover guard on the comparison pool
the installation month moved back 36 months, on every cell
Benjamini and Hochberg within each outcome, across subsets
25 treated units, below which a cell is not read
specifications.estimator_detail: Fit a Poisson model of the monthly count on an indicator for a treated unit after its installation month, with a fixed effect for every unit and a fixed effect for every calendar month, on the matched group panel, and take the exponential of that coefficient as the rate ratio. The variance is cluster robust of type CRV1, clustered on the match group, so a treated unit and its comparison intersections form one cluster. The installation month itself is dropped, because it is partly treated. A fit that returns a rate ratio outside 0.01 to 100 is refused as separation rather than reported.
specifications.placebo_detail: The placebo moves the installation month back by 36 months and reruns the same specification, so every month it uses falls strictly before installation and the honest answer is no effect. A placebo that rejects no effect at 5 per cent says the treated corners and their comparison locations were already drifting apart, and the estimate beside it is measuring that drift.
specifications.coverage: every subset and every outcome that identifies
specifications.reimplement: src/stats_subsets.py, which calls src/design_path.py poisson() and src/v6_models.py fit()
specifications.gate: A cell is read as a finding when three things hold together: (i) it is significant after Benjamini and Hochberg within its outcome, (ii) its placebo is consistent with no effect, and (iii) it carries at least the minimum unit count. A cell that fails any of the three is reported with the reason rather than dropped.
specifications.comparison_rule: The design this project has used throughout. Every universe intersection that survives the exclusion screen enters a pool. A treated unit is placed in a coarse exact stratum on four keys, borough, approach count clipped to 3 to 6, posted speed bucketed at 25, 30 and above 30, and the major leg flag, and the three pool members of that stratum closest to it in Mahalanobis distance are taken as controls. The distance is computed on four numbers per unit, all crashes and pedestrian crashes within 30 m annualised over months t0 minus 36 to t0 minus 25 and again over t0 minus 24 to t0 minus 13, so the slope of crash history is balanced and not only its level. The final pre treatment year is left out of the matching so it stays available as an out of sample placebo. Implemented by calling src/v6_panel2012.match(), not by a second copy.
specifications.comparison_exclusion: A pool member must have no treatment of any family from data/treatments.csv within 30 m, measured to the published geometry, and must be at least 300 m from every treated unit of the subset being estimated, which is the spillover guard from EXP-06. clean_families narrows the first screen to named families.
vulnerable_to: selection on anything not in the four strata keys or the two history blocks; the hardened arm fails its own placebo under this design, which is what an unbalanced trend looks like
area wide shocks, because a control can sit kilometres away and need not share a neighbourhood, a bus route or a school
an unrecorded treatment in the pool, since the screen can only exclude what the inventory records

neither_is_correct: Neither design is better in general. Each attains approximately the nominal rejection rate in one regime of site selection and rejects far too often in the other, and each one's bias runs in the direction of the estimate it reports. The three column groups are three answers, and the calibration panel is what a reader needs in order to weigh them.

difference.label: a difference in counts per intersection per year
difference.reading: A value of -0.14 means 0.14 fewer per intersection per year at treated corners than at their comparison locations.

ratio.label: a rate ratio
ratio.reading: A value of 0.90 means 10 per cent fewer at treated corners than at their comparison locations.

scales.warning: A rate ratio and a difference in counts are never comparable in magnitude. No effect is 1 on one scale and 0 on the other.
